scope: Native Radius custom Server/Settings device/browser login and live P composition in the existing encrypted registry slot

requirements.requirement: Usable explicit native Server/Settings issuer without a competing builtin or API-key flattening
requirements.implementation: Existing custom radius records own their configured gateway, stable credentialId and provider-secrets.enc slot. prepareRadiusOAuth reserves Core encrypted publication before issuer I/O. Existing OAuth service accepts the Core fixed-client device flow or browser full-redirect paste, not a Server listener/opener or caller token endpoint. API routes retain credentials capability, request lifetime and providerOperation leases. Settings custom cards expose Device connect/reconnect and Browser PKCE without selecting a model/provider. Public status is metadata only; an uncredentialed Radius adapter is not mounted or reported connected.
requirements.proof: New service9/registry11 cases and one actual authenticated HTTP scenario; one actual built-Server/static-Web Chromium journey creates the record, performs PKCE paste, imports real account config, explicitly configures defaults, infers P, reloads history and disconnects. Synthetic user capability403 and pending rename409 are explicit HTTP assertions.

requirements.implementation: Core readStoredCredential returns a defensive process-private administration snapshot, including expired data, without environment/commands/refresh/I/O or request authority. Registry uses validated snapshots only to bootstrap cache metadata; actual P operations resolve issuer-bound credentials with gateway/caller/refresh permission and revalidate current record, stable identity and headers before/after resolution. Metadata/header edits do not write an old OAuth token over a fresh refresh. Explicit key replacement remains separate. Rollback uses encrypted revision/CAS and refuses to overwrite a newer owner.
requirements.proof: Administrative snapshot test asserts no fetch/write and no allowRefresh:false availability for expired data. Registry fixture covers live refresh, header/token preservation, stale-handle refusal, same-grant cache/reload, foreign gateway and three failed-metadata rollback paths plus newer-writer refusal. Real HTTP expires the encrypted token, restarts Server, refreshes once, edits metadata, resumes private P history and proves the rotated credential is retained.

requirements.requirement: No late publication, stale admission or credential resurrection
requirements.implementation: Registry pending owners bind source identity and record fingerprint; update/disconnect/delete withdraw them, unchanged reload remains eligible and pending rename refuses. Publication preflights the native cache before mutation and returns a separately guarded synchronous admit closure; the flow owner checks again after await. An already committed grant is not erased merely because its helper returns after shutdown. Pre-aborted replacement requests cannot cancel an existing flow or leak an owner. Service/body/expiry/shutdown cancellation reuses Core ownership. Settings preserves the existing selection guard and falls back to global metadata reads after a stale/failed initial canonical reconcile.
requirements.proof: Held token responses are retired on replacement/disconnect/shutdown; caller cancellation releases a late body. Registry tests cover unsafe-cache byte preservation and final-owner refusal. Actual HTTP disconnect closes a held token body, leaves cache bytes unchanged, removes encrypted credentials and refuses inference; a cancelled browser callback also refuses. The original full-document Settings navigation now passes after the metadata-only fallback; existing late-rename/canonical-ID and passive-paste browser controls remain green.

requirements.requirement: Useful native P tool/private continuation and bounded affected-host regression
requirements.implementation: Existing P encoder, grant-owned continuation/cache, agent loop and durable session mechanisms are reused, not redelivered under MOD-03. Radius credentials are never passed as another issuer/API key. Shared paste help is loopback-neutral in EN/FR.
requirements.proof: Actual HTTP runs P→codemode→P, then refreshed/restarted P with the exact private tool/thinking fields, one tool and30 observed session tokens. Journals/public state/metadata/encrypted bytes do not expose synthetic credentials or tenant header. Existing API-key P, CLI print/JSON/RPC API-key and native OAuth, Codex HTTP and Web lifecycle-service checks pass separately.
